Sixteen comments

Also from O’Neill’s “Dance Music of Ireland”

↳ Posted by Musicalbison on June 9th, 2002.

This is often played as a Highland, or a Scottish. Dot the down beat, and cut the up beat in half throughout, like a hornpipe, but with harder syncopation.

↳ Posted by grymater on June 30th, 2004.

This is also played in American old-time circles. I have heard it most often played in G major.

↳ Posted by tedium on December 31st, 2005.

This reminds me of The Chicago Reel: https://thesession.org/tunes/840

↳ Posted by slainte on December 31st, 2005.

Bluegrass enthusiasts here in Kansas have been playing this tune in D (major). A group called “The Wilders” recorded a version recently, they play it up-tempo syncopated and then drift into straight meter, returning to the syncopation for the final go ’round.

↳ Posted by nmusser on January 12th, 2006.

Polly Put The Kettle On

My version with some variations of the old children’s song Polly Put The Kettle. This is a good piping version as lots of crans.

↳ Posted by JACKB on May 15th, 2014.

Molly Put The Kettle On, X:5

This nice old tune came to my mind today, so I thought I would check the versions here.
None of them seemed quite the way I had always played it. I don’t remember who’s version I learned.
Maybe it was Martin Connolly? Anyway this version is a straightforward reel with lots of triplets to drive it along.
It was one of the first reels I learned on B/C accordion. I have switched to C#/D now, so I prefer this reel on concertina.
The (3cec triplet --which is what concertina players use-- can be replaced with whatever short roll or cran you can make on a c-natural.
